subject: Medford Social Service Programs and Resources
overview: Social Service Coordinator Jason Stone discussed the diverse health and outreach programs offered by the Medford Health Department. The interview detailed resource navigation for mental health, recovery support, and the operational challenges posed by the regional housing crisis.

items.title: Introduction to Guest Jason Stone
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced Jason Stone, who has served as the city's Social Service Coordinator since November 2024.

items.title: Professional Background
items.summary: Stone detailed his twenty-year career in substance use disorder and community corrections before transitioning into municipal social services in Wakefield and Medford.

items.title: Health Department Overview
items.summary: The Medford Health Department manages core municipal functions including inspectional services, environmental health, public health nursing, and animal control.

items.title: Office of Prevention and Outreach
items.summary: The Office of Prevention and Outreach (OPO) utilizes grant funding to provide specialized health equity coordinators, recovery coaches, and community connectors.

items.title: Social Service Program Subdivisions
items.summary: The department is organized into three primary areas focusing on mental health and substance abuse, the Medford Connects engagement team, and school-based prevention programs.

items.title: Navigation and Triage Process
items.summary: Stone explained his role as a resource connector who helps residents navigate complex systems like MassHealth and social security during personal crises.

items.title: Trends in Mental Health Awareness
items.summary: The discussion addressed the surge in mental health service demand, attributed to reduced social stigma, increased diagnostic awareness, and the long-term impacts of the pandemic.

items.title: Community Liaison and Recovery Groups
items.summary: Specialized liaisons conduct cultural outreach for Haitian, Brazilian, and Arabic-speaking communities while hosting recovery groups and financial literacy events.

items.title: Emergency and Inter-Departmental Response
items.summary: The social services team collaborates with police-embedded mental health clinicians and local emergency services to triage crisis situations involving community safety.

items.title: Housing Crisis and Operational Challenges
items.summary: The coordinator identified the regional lack of affordable housing as the city's most significant social challenge, as many residents exceed income limits for traditional aid but cannot afford market rents.

items.title: Public Contact Information and Office Hours
items.summary: Residents can access services via the City Hall office, the Medford Health Department website, or during weekly open office hours at the public library.
